cells.tense: The structure is going up now and the pen is in your hand.
cells.act: show someone the way you found
cells.ask: Someone near you is stuck on a route you already worked out the hard way. Say the way through, plainly, once — then let them take it at their own pace.
cells.core: When something new has to get built, you can already see the route — not because you were told, but because you cleared the ground yourself and the structure took what you learned. That is the working face of this: the passage in your mind becoming a passage somebody else can use. It is not force and it is not the answer you arrived at; it is the direction, offered plainly. There is a way through something near you that has stalled at the improvising stage, and the next move is to make it repeatable, not more exciting. Say the route once. Watch how they take it; if the direction was theirs, it will still be theirs. What you hand over comes back as the shape of it.
cells.sheetLine: You can hand someone the way you found.
cells.verb: building something new from what the clearing revealed
cells.place: where things get weighed back into proportion

cells.tense: Something is being built ahead in your mind and none of it has happened yet.
cells.act: leave the hollow ritual for the living one
cells.ask: Find the form you keep performing out of habit — the standing arrangement, the role, the shaped answer. Do the version that still connects you to the people in it, and drop the hollow one, that once.
cells.core: The structure is going up in your head first, at a scale whose end you cannot see. Building turns into keeping it possible — one more revision, one more route nobody has to walk yet — while the version already running is not treated as done. What was going to be made has turned into a way of not arriving. Notice where a thing you do has gone form without meaning: the role, the meeting, the shape that is expected. For one of them, do the living version and skip the hollow one. Nothing has to be torn down. You only have to touch what still connects. The rest can stand unexamined a while further.

cells.tense: Something was already built and it stands behind you while you wait.
cells.act: make the call and carry it through
cells.ask: A decision keeps being restaged — asked again, weighed again — waiting for the answer to feel right. Decide it today, do it today, skip the explaining afterward. One motion, not two.
cells.core: The structure is there. It was built, it holds, and the work now is to keep it usable — and where you build with others, you have started waiting for the room to authorise the next move. The waiting got called patience. What is actually missing is a call: not a bigger one, just this one, decided and carried the same day. Once the action is out, the room has something to hold instead of a plan. You do not need to feel clear before you move; the moving is where the clarity shows up. Make it and carry it, and see how the ground answers.

cells.tense: A structure is already standing under your hands and the name on it is wrong.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: Expect a lean this week — a question, a push, someone acting as if your direction chose itself. Answer with the direction, not a defence. Hold once, and skip the account keeping.
cells.core: You are building, and it is going the way you chose long back — but the account of it says it happened by itself, or by circumstance, or because someone else steered. The momentum is gathered and doing its job; what is missing is the one who gathered it. So the structure keeps getting defended against tests it should not have had to pass. There is a direction of yours being carried, and someone will lean on it. Hold the heading once. Not with an argument — with the direction itself. You do not have to explain that it was yours. Keep going that way; the story will sort itself out later.
cells.sheetLine: It keeps being carried, and nobody knows who chose.

attempts.check: The one unsupported claim in the draft is that the person is building something with others — the record says Formation's structure is 'the first raised by more than one pair of hands,' but nothing in the record tells me this person's build is collaborative, or that a specific someone is waiting for a share. The reader could reasonably say 'no, this is my own work, no one else is in it.' The ask survives that: in Balanced it is Guidance (show someone the way you found), which needs a second person only as the one being shown the route — if the wrong read holds, they can be shown to themselves, but the record does allow another person as part of this act since Guidance is about people; heed the plan's clause. In Too Much the ask is Passage (leave the hollow ritual for the living one), which needs no name. In Too Little and Unacknowledged the medicines are the person's own and need no one. The sentence that serves me more than the person is 'something is being built that couldn't exist before old structures were cleared' — it flatters the reading; I keep it out.
